claims.wording: The author describes analysis as the main purpose and advises against indiscriminate cache deletion.
claims.excerpt: I wrote this app just for fast analysing purposes. the cleaning option was just a handy extra feature. I do not recommend you to delete your cache files.
claims.scope: Not a benchmark or universal claim that cache removal never helps

claims.wording: The documented Analyse flow skips protected files and can display 0 MB when the administrator password is not supplied.
claims.excerpt: If you do not provide the password, Clean Me will just skip those files for which it requires root and display 0 MB.
claims.scope: 0 MB is not proof that the folder is empty; do not request credentials or advise granting permissions automatically

claims.wording: The documented Clean action deletes selected topics; folder icons open the corresponding folders for inspection.
claims.excerpt: Click Clean to delete all topics that are selected ... Click the little folder icon to open the specific folder which will be cleaned.
claims.scope: Category selection is not per-file review, rollback, Trash-only handling or a safety guarantee

claims.wording: The author says Clean Me clears directory contents rather than deleting the directory itself; iMessage attachment removal requires Full Disk Access.
claims.excerpt: Only the content of the directory will be cleaned ... To be able to remove iMessage attachments, Clean Me requires full disk access.
claims.scope: Not independently audited; do not turn permission instructions into a recommendation to grant access

claims.wording: The author documents local directory analysis and says Clean Me normally should not request an internet connection.

workflowArticle.title: Clean Me shows 0 MB: check permissions before cleanup
workflowArticle.primaryIntent: Interpret Clean Me's documented permission-dependent scan results without assuming zero means empty or granting blanket deletion authority.
workflowArticle.descriptionDirection: Explain that Clean Me documents skipped protected files as 0 MB; distinguish analysis from cleanup and state the archived/Catalina scope before offering a modern preview alternative.
outline: Top: official Clean Me screenshot with historical/version-unknown caption
0 MB can mean an unscanned protected category, not an empty folder (CM07)
Open the folder and review categories before considering Clean (CM08); personal Downloads/attachments are not disposable cache
Treat cache sizes and rebuild cost as separate decisions; author discourages broad cache deletion (CM06)
Do not infer current macOS support or a working Homebrew install from old documentation (CM02-CM04, CM12)
Later: current-source Breathing Room Space example preview; bounded disclosed alternative with preview, Python, hosted AI and pricing caveats (BR01-BR03)
Finish with a permission/inspection/backup decision checklist, not an install or cleanup command
workflowArticle.interactionPass: Plan a static decision aid: Was the category scanned? If permission was declined, label size unknown; inspect folder where accessible; decide whether data is reproducible and backed up; leave unverified data untouched. No permission changes or filesystem actions.
workflowArticle.distinctness: The article resolves a specific documented 0 MB ambiguity; comparison page instead answers product choice. No duplicate alternatives route.

comparison.title: Breathing Room vs Clean Me: scope and preview limits
comparison.primaryIntent: Choose between an archived category-based Mac analyser and a broader maintenance preview without mistaking unknown features for absences.
comparison.leadDirection: Clean Me documents direct category inspection/cleanup with an MIT licence; Breathing Room, which we build, adds source-implemented storage/process/approval workflows but has material preview and hosted-service caveats.
rows: documented local operation versus optional hosted AI
process grouping and recurring growth: unknown for Clean Me
comparison.visualPlan: Same two sourced product views with captions and licence notice, not stock imagery or a generated UI.
comparison.lengthRule: Concise sourced decision matrix; do not expand into a second workflow article.

cleanMe: MIT source and explicit category/folder inspection are useful for understanding this older workflow (CM05, CM08).
Author's caution against routine cache deletion provides a useful boundary (CM06).
Archived repository, Catalina-scoped release, unverified modern runtime and broken checked cask endpoint limit installation recommendations (CM02-CM04, CM12).
Selection includes potentially valuable personal data; not a risk-free cleanup or automatic rollback claim (CM08-CM09).
breathingRoom: Source-implemented broader exploration, app/helper grouping and constrained approval records can fit a recurring-investigation job; binary feature parity remains unverified (BR03).
Free local app and optional advertised paid hosted care serve different needs (BR02).
Non-notarized preview, Python prerequisite, incomplete Intel/clean-machine QA and cloud authentication/data transfer are material disadvantages, not footnotes (BR01-BR02).
Neither screenshots nor source establish measured savings or comparative safety (BR03).
advantagesAndTradeoffs.editorialJudgment: A supported, independently validated modern utility or built-in inspection may be preferable when preview software and legacy compatibility uncertainty are unacceptable. Do not recommend granting access or running either cleaner merely for the article.
